_note: Two places where a gate may declare, as a visible ledger edit, a check that cannot fail in the tree's current state. `allowed` is the assertion-count budget for gate assertions whose first argument is the bare literal true: such an assertion can never fail — it inflates the declared count, satisfies gate-ratchet, and is invisible to gate-proven-red, so poisoning the guarded artefact fails the OTHER assertions instead. A count is not a check. Adding one to any gate without raising its number here fails gate-vacuity assertion 2; lowering a number here without removing the assertion fails assertion 3. `emptyPaths` declares a path that is deliberately empty — a tree that holds no documents (gate-docs, gate-tasks, preflight P-01/P-08) or a file that is intentionally absent (archive/MANIFEST.md, README.md, docs/phase-2/PHASE-2-GATE-SPECS.md, the four root documents). Without that declaration a gate which scans an empty corpus reports PASS having read nothing, and a gate which requires a file fails on one the repository chose to remove. Every entry needs path, owner and reason; an entry missing any of the three is not a declaration at all — the consuming gate still fails and names the malformed entry.

emptyPaths.reason: The Set-1 v2 instruction corpus under docs/phase-2 was removed from the repository on 2026-11-19 as part of the documentation purge (read every md/txt, apply the due instructions, then delete the markdown). gate-docs, gate-tasks and preflight P-01 consequently have no corpus to scan, to read tasks from, or to resolve paths against; this entry records that the emptiness is deliberate, so that a corpus which disappears by accident fails those gates instead of passing quietly.

The archive manifest was a markdown file and was removed by the documentation purge. preflight P-07 requires it so that nothing retired leaves the tree without a manifest row; the requirement is declared vacuous here rather than silently dropped.
Root document removed by the documentation purge. gate-hygiene requires the four root documents; their absence is declared here so the assertion keeps failing on an UNdeclared disappearance.

_why.gate-ratchet: The two assertions in the 'no .ratchet.json yet' early-return branch are literal-true on purpose and are the only legitimate case in the harness: on a first pass there is genuinely nothing to compare against, and the gate may not read a file that does not exist yet. They report the fixpoint ('nothing has regressed') and say so in their detail string. Every other literal-true assertion in any gate is padding, and is treated as such.
